record.paper_title: Twenty Open Questions in Supersymmetric Particle Physics
record.original_question: After supersymmetry breaking in the MSSM, quark and lepton mass eigenstates need not remain aligned with their squark and slepton partners, so gaugino interactions can generate flavor-changing neutral currents. What physical principle or mediation mechanism suppresses these supersymmetric flavor-changing effects, and does nature use scalar degeneracy and a super-GIM mechanism, alignment of fermion and scalar bases, decoupling of the first two scalar generations, gauge mediation, or some other realization?

evidence.quote: The Problem arises with gauginos, which couple to both a particle and its superpartner simultaneously. In this case the coupling has the form Ũ†U, which need not be diagonal. Thus gauginos can generate FCNC’s.
There are three primary proposals for solving the SUSY flavor problem: degeneracy, alignment, and decoupling.
Once SUSY is discovered, it may not take long to discern which of these paths nature has chosen to follow.

artifact.status_search_result: The supersymmetric flavor problem remains an open question because supersymmetry itself has not been discovered experimentally. Theoretical proposals (degeneracy / super-GIM, alignment, decoupling of first two generations, gauge mediation, anomaly/gaugino/flavor mediation, and hybrids) continue to be actively studied; recent (2024–2025) work, including string-landscape statistical arguments, favors mixed quasi-degeneracy/decoupling scenarios with multi-TeV first/second-generation scalars, but no mechanism has been confirmed by data. LHC searches have constrained but not selected among these options.

status_evidence.title: Living dangerously with decoupled first and second generation scalars
status_evidence.snippet: String landscape draws lead to a mixed quasidegeneracy/decoupling solution to the SUSY flavor and CP problems with first/second generation scalars in the 20–40 TeV range.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work still treats the SUSY flavor problem as an unresolved theoretical issue with competing proposed solutions.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting LHC constraints on gauge-mediated supersymmetry breaking
status_evidence.snippet: Gauge mediation provides a natural solution to the SUSY flavor problem; LHC searches constrain but do not confirm such scenarios.
status_evidence.claim: Gauge-mediation remains a viable but unverified candidate mechanism.

status_evidence.title: Flavor Mediation Delivers Natural SUSY
status_evidence.snippet: Higgsed gauge mediation combined with SM Yukawas yields degeneracy of first-two-generation scalars while allowing a lighter third generation.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple mediation schemes are actively proposed as competing solutions to the flavor problem.
